title: Transparent proxy mode: how the host is found from SNI or certificate

prose.text: In transparent mode the client does not know a proxy exists. {{how-it-works}}

prose.label: Finding the host.
prose.text: {{host-identification}} {{sni-example}} {{certificate-comes-later}} Whether a client can declare a different SNI to bypass policy is open {{gap:sni-spoofing}}. Whether the certificate fallback adds a round trip before the first decision is open {{gap:first-decision-latency}}.

prose.label: What changes for policy.
prose.text: Domain-based policy runs on the SNI before decryption: [[zia.ssl-inspection.pipeline]]. Destination IP is also matched in this mode, and its effect on exemptions is in [[zia.ssl-inspection.pipeline:transparent-matches-destination-ip]]; the IP-group criterion is in [[zia.ssl-inspection.criteria]].

prose.label: Identity and protocols.
prose.text: The client cannot answer a proxy 407, so user identity comes from Surrogate IP or Client Connector and otherwise from the location: [[zia.authentication.surrogate-ip]], [[zia.authentication.unauthenticated-traffic]]. Tunnels carry all ports and protocols ([[zia.traffic-forwarding.methods]]); IPv6 over IPSec needs explicit configuration ([[zia.traffic-forwarding.ipsec]]). What the router needs for GRE and IPSec is in [[zia.traffic-forwarding.gre]] and [[zia.traffic-forwarding.vpn-credentials]].

checks.do: Whether the client sends SNI, which a capture of the Client Hello shows, since the host is taken from SNI when it is present.
Whether any rule's outcome depends on the destination IP, since this mode matches on it.

how-it-works.statement: In transparent mode the browser has no proxy configured; traffic is directed to a Service Edge by other means, such as a GRE or IPSec tunnel at the organization's egress router, so the destination IP in the IP header is the origin server's address.

quotes: In Transparent mode, the browser is not configured to send traffic to a Service Edge.
such as a GRE or IPSec tunnel configured at your organization’s egress router
the destination IP address in the IP header of the request contains the IP address of the destination server.

host-identification.statement: The Service Edge identifies the destination host from the Server Name Indication extension in the TLS Client Hello when present, and otherwise from the server certificate sent during the SSL handshake.

quotes: Using the Server Name Indication (SNI) extension if the initial HTTPS request (client hello) includes SNI, which is an extension to the TLS protocol.
Using the server certificate sent by the destination server during the SSL handshake, if the HTTPS request does not include the SNI extension.

sni-example.statement: Most browsers send SNI when a server uses one certificate for several sites; for example, with a common *.google.com certificate the service can block drive.google.com while allowing mail.google.com and google.com.

quotes: Most browsers use SNI when a server uses a common certificate for multiple sites.
a Service Edge might use SNI to apply a policy to block traffic to drive.google.com, but allow traffic to mail.google.com and google.com.

certificate-comes-later.statement: The certificate fallback can only happen after the server has answered during the handshake, which is later than a CONNECT host or a Client Hello SNI.

quotes: Using the server certificate sent by the destination server during the SSL handshake, if the HTTPS request does not include the SNI extension.

certificate-comes-later.conditions: The ordering follows from where the certificate is sent; any latency or trust consequence is not stated.

sni-spoofing.title: SNI spoofing and the trust placed in the certificate
sni-spoofing.detail: Unverified legacy statement: A client could declare a different SNI than the site it connects to and bypass policy, SSL inspection mitigates this, and server-certificate identification trusts the server's self-reported identity. No captured source states it; a lab test would settle it.

first-decision-latency.title: Added delay when a transparent connection has no SNI
first-decision-latency.detail: Unverified legacy statement: The certificate fallback adds one round trip before the first policy decision. No captured source states it; a lab test would settle it.
